title: Topic Triage Agent output
description: Routing-only triage. Triage decides whether a candidate is important and verification-clear enough to deserve the expensive later-literature Research audit, and whether it must be decomposed. It does not produce the problem's verification contract: expected_result, answer_types, verification_standard, verification_difficulty, and the CI contract are produced by the Research Agent (see schemas/stages/research-topic.schema.json). The screening benchmark measures those judgments separately under schemas/screening/prediction.schema.json.

importance_level.description: Only high or medium importance proceeds to the expensive later-literature Research audit, so this is a real gate with downstream consequences, not a decorative label.

verification_clarity.description: clear only when an unambiguous acceptance condition can be stated for the source-faithful question. needs_decomposition or unverifiable require at least one proposed subproblem.

decomposition_parent_coverage.description: not_applicable when verification is clear and no subproblems are proposed; complete when component children collectively cover the parent; partial otherwise. A restricted_derived child always retains the parent and cannot use complete.

proposed_subproblems.description: Empty when verification_clarity is clear; at least one source-faithful subproblem otherwise. Each subproblem either decomposes immediately in this run or enters the persistent topic queue for later campaign rounds.

assessment.description: Free-form screening narrative passed to the Research Agent as context: why the candidate matters, what solving it would change, why verification is clear or not, and any mismatch between the candidate and a famous/named formulation. This is context for the next stage, not a machine-consumed contract.
